clusters.merge_notes: All 4 are Stop hooks with an identical skeleton: read transcript_path (or JSON payload) → extract last assistant text (+ tool_use count for verify-basis) → regex-match a 'confidence/completion claim' → require an 'evidence token' set → block or advise. CONFLICT: silent-claim-drift-gate scans the whole stringified payload (looser, cheaper, catches skill-invocation + arch-doc drift too) while the other 3 parse transcript_path and isolate the LAST assistant text specifically — a merge must standardize on the transcript_path parse (more precise) and keep silent-claim-drift's extra payload-wide checks (skill-token, HYPOTHESIS ratio, arch-doc-sync) as separate sub-checks since they aren't claim/evidence shaped. SHARED PREDICATE SHAPE: 'claim regex fired + evidence/backing regex absent (or tools=0) → block/advise'; ticket-criteria-gate CHECK C and veritas CHECK2 overlap semantically (both demand runtime proof for a 'verified/saved/persists' claim) — merged gate should dedupe these into one BEHAVIOURAL/VERIFIED-CLAIM branch with the union of both evidence-token sets (RUNTIME_EVIDENCE ∪ REPRO_BEFORE ∪ EVIDENCE_TOKEN). A single merged gate MUST preserve: (1) the 3 distinct block-vs-advisory severities (veritas CHECK1 hard, others hard, veritas CHECK2/3 + drift + checklist advisory) — do not flatten to one severity; (2) each hook's own EXEMPT/ABSTAIN regex set (they differ slightly — FRAME_ABSTAIN vs ABSTAIN vs none) unioned, not replaced; (3) distinct bypass tokens per original check (skip-veritas / skip-verify-basis / skip-criteria-gate / skip-invoke / skip-100-verify / skip-architecture-doc-update) all still recognized so existing muscle-memory bypasses keep working; (4) separate log files (or one shared ledger with a 'source' field) since each currently logs to its own path and audits key off that.

clusters.merge_notes: 4 of 5 are Stop hooks sharing the identical 'read last assistant text from transcript_path, regex-match a shape-violation signal, hard-block with a reason list' skeleton; PlainFirstGate is structurally different — it is a UserPromptSubmit hook gating on MIYA's incoming prompt shape, not Ruri's outgoing reply, and its output is raw stdout text rather than the hookSpecificOutput/decision JSON envelope the Stop hooks use. CONFLICT: terse-gate (>150-char lines) and show-gate (missing box/fence on a 'comparison' signal) and full-address-trace-gate (bad file:line refs) can all fire on the SAME reply simultaneously (e.g. a long prose reply describing a before/after fix with bad file refs) — currently each is an independent Stop hook so Claude Code likely runs them in sequence per settings.json array order, meaning a merged gate must decide fire-order or emit a single combined block reason rather than 3 sequential blocks. show-gate and full-address-trace-gate and stop-point-summary all use the SAME EXEMPT/ban-structure literals (═══, るり結界, 'Domain Expansion' banner) — a merge should unify this into one shared EXEMPT regex constant. stop-point-summary is the ODD ONE for bypass semantics: it explicitly REJECTS free-text bypasses (all others accept any free-text reason after the colon) — a merged gate must preserve this whitelist-vs-freetext distinction per sub-check, not average it into one universal bypass grammar. A single merged reply-shape gate must preserve: severity is uniformly hard-block for the 4 Stop hooks (safe to merge into one decision:block emission point) but PlainFirstGate's pre-emit advisory nature and prompt-side trigger axis must stay a SEPARATE hook (different event type, different subject of the check) — do not fold it into the Stop-side merge.

clusters.merge_notes: This cluster is the most heterogeneous — 3 UserPromptSubmit reminders (route-consult-gate, codemap-recon-consult.trigger, skill-invocation-discipline-gate), 3 PreToolUse Edit|Write gates (design-consult-gate, pre-action-check-gate, meta-edit-gate), and 1 Stop back-gate (codemap-recon-consult.discipline). CONFLICT/OVERLAP 1: design-consult-gate and meta-edit-gate BOTH hard-block edits to overlapping path sets (hooks/*.js, skills SKILL.md, domain *.hook.js, settings.json, quest-protocol.md) but check DIFFERENT prerequisites — design-consult-gate requires system-design + system-rules skill invocation, meta-edit-gate requires meta/system-architecture.md having been Read/Edited this session (arch-doc-sync). Both fire independently on the SAME edit today (e.g. editing a hook triggers both denies in sequence if neither prerequisite is met) — a merge must keep BOTH prerequisite checks (they are NOT redundant: one is 'did you consult the design skills', the other is 'did you touch the architecture doc') but could combine them into a single deny message listing both missing items rather than two sequential PreToolUse denials. CONFLICT/OVERLAP 2: codemap-recon-consult.trigger.hook.js (UserPromptSubmit, state-driven off active.txt phase) and codemap-recon-consult.discipline.hook.js (Stop, claim-driven) are an intentional front-gate/back-gate PAIR for the same underlying rule (consult codegraph/BPMN during investigation) — these two should NOT be merged into one hook since they fire on different events (prompt-time reminder vs Stop-time enforcement) but SHOULD stay paired/adjacent in any reorganization; the discipline hook additionally carries 2 unrelated sub-rules bolted on later (git-history probe, UI .xhtml-citation requirement) that a merge should consider splitting into their own named checks since they don't share the 'consult codegraph' predicate at all. CONFLICT 3: pre-action-check-gate's quest-path pattern set (1. Tasks\Melaka, QA-NNN active folder, active.txt, etanah src) partially overlaps design-consult-gate's ETANAH_PATHS advisory (etanah-*/src/*.java) — both can fire on the same etanah Java edit, one as a quest-context checklist reminder and the other as a system-design new-symbol advisory; they check DIFFERENT things (pre-action = quest hygiene, design-consult = architectural consult) so should stay separate but a merged gate registry should document that an etanah edit can legitimately trigger both. A single merged consult-router must preserve: the front/back-gate pairing pattern (reminder-then-enforce) as a template rather than collapsing to one; the distinct HARD-BLOCK-vs-advisory severity per original check (2 blocking PreToolUse gates + 1 blocking Stop gate + 4 pure-advisory reminders); and every hook's own bypass token namespace (skip-design-consult / skip-eval-check / skip-codegraph / skip-git-history / skip-canonical-doc / skip-architecture-doc-update) since みや and Ruri already use these in transcripts and a rename would break audit greps.

clusters.merge_notes: These two are near-duplicate siblings by design (per quest-active-grounding.js header comment: 'Pairs with mode-detector.js') — both are UserPromptSubmit hooks that independently read the SAME quest/active.txt file, parse it with functionally-identical parseBlocks/fieldOf/blockHasQA/isPastTesting logic (mode-detector.js:44-77 vs quest-active-grounding.js:41-85 are near line-for-line copies), and apply the IDENTICAL 'active AND NOT (phase=1 AND local_test_confirmed)' predicate. CONFLICT: none semantically — they answer different questions (mode-detector: WHICH abstract mode am I in, single aggregate label, ALWAYS prints even when Discussion; quest-active-grounding: WHAT are the concrete active quests' scope/phase details, per-quest lines, SILENT when none match) — but the duplicated active.txt-parsing code is pure waste: two separate file reads + two separate block-parsers running on every single prompt for overlapping output. A merged gate should: (1) parse active.txt ONCE, (2) emit mode-detector's one-line abstract label ALWAYS (even 'Discussion'), (3) THEN append quest-active-grounding's per-quest detail lines only when quest-active blocks exist, producing a single combined UserPromptSubmit emission instead of two separate hook invocations with duplicated file I/O and block-parsing logic. Must preserve: mode-detector's unconditional-emit behavior (downstream mode-scoped rules like operational-follow-through.js key off the literal '🎯 Mode: Quest-active' string being present every turn, per its own header comment) and quest-active-grounding's silence-when-empty behavior (its header explicitly calls this out as intentional, 'don't noise the prompt') — these are NOT the same behavior and collapsing them incorrectly would either spam Discussion-mode prompts with empty grounding lines or silently drop the always-on mode label.
